items.title: Restored panes pick up where the program left off
items.text: After re-attaching, a pane's cursor could be left near the right edge, so the next line of output started in the wrong column and a later restore could repeat a line. The cursor now lands exactly where the program left it.

items.title: The background process no longer grows without limit
items.text: If the app stopped reading for a while (suspended, or behind a slow connection), the background process kept queueing every byte your panes printed until it could run out of memory and take every session with it. It now holds a bounded amount and catches the app up, in order, once it is reading again.

items.title: No more frozen panes on bursts of terminal queries
items.text: A program sending many terminal queries at once could freeze its pane for seconds and lose the replies. Those bursts are now answered immediately.

items.title: Survives running out of file handles
items.text: The background process keeps running and retries when the system is briefly out of file handles, instead of exiting and ending your sessions.
